page: OVHcloud c2-30 is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs, utilizing an Intel Haswell processor running at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz. The CPU configuration does not use hyperthreading, providing a 1.0 thread-per-core ratio. The system is equipped with 30.0 GB of system memory, translating to 3.75 GB of RAM per core, and includes 200 GB of local SSD storage.

Benchmark results indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core performance is relatively low, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance falling into the bottom 10% and Geekbench single-core scores in the bottom 25%. However, multi-core benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU tests, consistently rank in the middle 50% (average). Memory bandwidth tests show average read performance for both cached and uncached blocks, though uncached write bandwidth is weaker, placing in the bottom 25%.

Given the dedicated core allocation and average multi-threaded capabilities, the c2-30 is suited for parallelizable workloads that do not rely heavily on single-thread execution speeds. It performs adequately in software compilation, ray tracing, and static web serving, all of which score in the average tier. It is also capable of handling database operations and Redis SET operations at average performance levels. However, it is less suited for cryptography, text processing, or large-scale LLM inference, where benchmarks show weak or unavailable performance.
